# Temple Scroll Column 13 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** 11Q19 (Cave 11), Col. 13 | **Condition:** fragmentary

---

**13:1** [...] on the fifteenth day of the seventh month [...]

**13:2** [...] when you gather in the produce of the land [...]

**13:3** [...] you shall celebrate a festival to the LORD seven days [...]

**13:4** [...] on the first day a holy convocation; all laborious work you shall not do [...]

**13:5** [...] a festival of booths it is, seven days to the LORD [...]

**13:6** [...] you shall bring near a burnt offering, a fire offering of soothing aroma to the LORD [...]

**13:7** [...] thirteen young bulls, sons of the herd, two rams, fourteen lambs, sons of a year, without blemish [...]

**13:8** [...] and their grain offerings and their drink offerings for the bulls, for the rams, and for the lambs [...]

**13:9** [...] according to their number, according to the ordinance [...]

**13:10** [...] and one male goat for a sin offering, besides the perpetual burnt offering [...]

**13:11** [...] its grain offering and its drink offering [...]

**13:12** [...] and you shall dwell in booths seven days [...]

**13:13** [...] every native in Israel shall dwell in booths [...]

**13:14** [...] so that your generations shall know that in booths I caused the sons of Israel to dwell [...]

**13:15** [...] when I brought them out from the land of Egypt [...]

**13:16** [...] and you shall rejoice before Me seven days; a statute forever throughout your generations [...]

---

*EMET notes: Column 13 is fragmentary but preserves the core Festival of Booths (chag ha-sukkot) legislation. Content parallels Numbers 29:12-16 and Leviticus 23:33-43. The first day prescribes thirteen bulls — the highest number in the graduated Sukkot offering sequence. "Caused to dwell" preserves the Hif'il of yashav. The rationale clause (dwelling in booths as memorial of the Exodus) follows Leviticus 23:42-43.*
